inventory.pattern: object pronoun after a preposition (with me / for him)
inventory.gap: wrote 'with I trying to learn'; nouns hide it, only pronouns expose it
inventory.example: With me being the only reviewer, it took a week.

inventory.pattern: purpose nouns (a learning system, not a system for learning)
inventory.gap: reaches for 'a platform where we can...' or a bare noun; never stacks the purpose noun in front. 0 uses in 45 exchanges
inventory.example: Rednote is a great recipe-sharing platform.

inventory.pattern: fronted participle clause (Looking at his watch, he saw...)
inventory.gap: the same-subject half of P001, named in drill 01 but never drilled; uses a finite clause or 'when I...' instead. E053/E011/E005 all show participle-vs-finite confusion
inventory.example: Sitting in the library, I can actually focus.

inventory.gap: reaches for 'all ... not' to mean total negation, which English reads as partial (all users couldn't pay = not all could); the none-of frame has never been used
inventory.example: None of the users could pay.

inventory.pattern: post-noun modifier hangers: with + feature, in + clothing, -ing + action, place phrase last
inventory.gap: Chinese stacks every modifier before the noun (的-chains); English says the head noun first and hangs modifiers after it. He assembles in Chinese order and either stalls or builds a noun pile ('the unit of the amount saved in database', Day 24). Learner-raised gap.
inventory.example: the guy with long hair and glasses, in a black jersey, playing on the court over there

inventory.pattern: stacked time adverbials, small-to-large with zero extra prepositions (at 6:30 on Friday morning last week)
inventory.gap: writes 'At midnight of last Saturday' - inserts of between date and clock time, and adds on/in before last/this/next which license none. English chains time phrases like an address, small unit first, each part keeping its own preposition (at + clock, on + date-bound morning, in + bare morning), and last/this/next/yesterday strip all prepositions.
inventory.example: The alert fired at 9:40 on Monday night, and by midnight last Saturday we had rolled it back.

inventory.pattern: abstract prepositions by spatial metaphor: on = surface/line, in = container, of = part-whole
inventory.gap: default-preposition guessing under abstraction: knows at/on/in for physical space but treats abstract objects (a line of code, a file, the morning, a topic) as random slots. The fix is not memorizing collocations but projecting the physical prototype: a line of text is a LINE (on), a file is a CONTAINER (in), a root cause is a PART (of). Learner-raised gap from the on/in/of QA (Day 33).
inventory.example: leave a comment on that line / the bug in this function / the root cause of the incident

inventory.gap: packs a secondary fact into the main sentence instead of a separate short clause; never used in 45 exchanges
inventory.example: With everyone booking at once, tickets are impossible.

inventory.pattern: the more X, the more Y (correlative comparative)
inventory.gap: says two separate sentences or an if-clause for a proportional link; 0 uses in 55 exchanges across 11 days
inventory.example: The longer the commute, the less I want to go in.

inventory.gap: concedes with a separate sentence or drops it; 0 uses in 55 exchanges. E011 shows the same clause defect one level up (Whenever working from home)
inventory.example: No matter how bad the traffic is, I still drive back.

inventory.gap: always spells the clause out in full (who is responsible / which was unrelated); such clauses are grammatically fine, so nothing ever errors and the reduced form has never once appeared. The trap runs the other way - dropping who + a lexical verb
inventory.example: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.

inventory.pattern: the object or idea as the subject, not 'I + verb' (passive / fronted subject)
inventory.gap: every sentence about a thing or wish opens with 'I + verb'; the object or idea is never placed in subject position. Not grammar - nothing ever errors - the fronted-subject frame simply never surfaces. Same recall gap as C031, one level up: C031 is a noun slot, this is a whole-sentence frame.
inventory.example: I follow the rule strictly. -> The rule gets followed strictly. / I want to read books before bed. -> Books before bed are still the plan.

inventory.gap: renders Chinese de-chains word by word as 'the A of the B saved in C'; when the head noun is an information point (unit/name/reason/time/way), English reaches for an embedded question instead - a frame he already owns ('find out what the problem was', Day 24) but the de-chain still wins under production pressure
inventory.example: the unit of the amount saved in database -> what unit the amount was stored in

cards.cue: 大家都挤在同一时间订票，火车票根本抢不到。
cards.task: Everyone books at the same time. It is impossible to get train tickets.
cards.answer: With everyone booking at the same time, it's impossible to get train tickets.
cards.said: It's impossible to get train tickets with everyone booking at the same time.
cards.why: Structure correct. Position is a separate habit - see What Went Wrong.

cards.cue: 父母家四小时车程，回一趟就把整个周末吃掉了。
cards.task: My parents are four hours away. A trip back eats the whole weekend.
cards.answer: With my parents four hours away, a trip back eats the whole weekend.
cards.said: A trip back eats the whole weekend with my parents four hours away.
cards.why: No participle needed here - an adjective phrase attaches directly. Handled correctly.

cards.cue: 工作和学新东西占掉了大部分时间，现在看小说算是奢侈了。
cards.task: Work and new things take up most of my time. Reading a novel is a luxury these days.
cards.answer: With work and new things taking up most of my time, reading a novel is a luxury these days.
cards.said: Reading a novel is a luxury these days with work and new things taking up most my time.
cards.why: Structure correct. `most my time` -> `most of my time` is not the pattern and was not counted.

cards.cue: 我想学的东西太多，红色警戒一直拖着没玩。
cards.task: I have got so much I am trying to learn. I never get round to Red Alert.
cards.answer: With so much I'm trying to learn, I never get round to Red Alert.
cards.said: I never get round to Red Alert with I trying to learn so much.
cards.why: `with` is a preposition, so a pronoun after it takes the object form - `with me trying`, never `with I trying`. Nouns hide this because they do not inflect, which is why only this item exposed it. Smoother still: `with so much on my plate`.

cards.cue: 短裤卖完了，最后我只买了水果就走了。
cards.task: The shorts were sold out. I ended up leaving with just the fruit.
cards.answer: With the shorts sold out, I ended up leaving with just the fruit.
cards.said: I ended up leaving with just the fruit with the shorts sold out.
cards.why: Form correct. But this item forces the front position: the sentence already contains a real preposition `with just the fruit`, so trailing the pattern puts two unrelated `with`s in one sentence and the listener has to work out which is which.

cards.cue: 大家都在家办公，办公室里冷清得很。
cards.task: Everyone was working from home. The office felt dead.
cards.answer: The office felt dead with everyone working from home.
cards.said: The office felt dead with everyone working from home.
cards.why: Active, so `-ing`. Correct.

cards.cue: 短信服务商正在更换中，所以我得把每个地方都测一遍。
cards.task: The SMS provider is being swapped out right now. I have got to test everything.
cards.answer: With the SMS provider being swapped out right now, I've got to test everything.
cards.said: With the SMS provider being swapped out right now, I've got to test everyting.
cards.why: The hardest item in the drill - passive and still in progress, so `being` is required. Identified unprompted.

cards.cue: 截止时间改到了周三，市场部就不再催我了。
cards.task: The deadline has been moved to Wednesday. Marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.answer: With the deadline moved to Wednesday, marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.said: With the deadline moved to Wednesday, marketing has stopped chasing me.
cards.why: Passive but finished, so no `being`. The contrast with item 3 is the whole point of the round, and both were judged correctly.

cards.cue: 大家都挤在同一周抢票，所以我宁愿开车回去也不坐车。
cards.task: Someone asks why you drive home for National Day instead of taking the train. Use the pattern, with "everyone squeezed into the same week" as the background.
cards.answer: With everyone buying train tickets in the same week, I'd rather drive back than take the train.
cards.said: With everyone buying train tickets at the same week, I prefer driving car back rather than taking train.
cards.why: Pattern correct. `at the same week` -> `in the same week` and the missing article in `driving car back` are ordinary chat repairs, not the pattern, and were not counted here.

cards.cue: 因为动到了核心逻辑，我估得得一周左右。
cards.task: You are explaining to a colleague why the ticket needs a week, with "the core logic was touched" as the background.
cards.answer: With the core logic touched, I'd put it closer to a week.
cards.said: With the core logic touched, I'd put it closer to a week.
cards.why: Passive and finished, so no `being` - correct. `I'd put it closer to a week` is `C024`, produced with no prompting.

cards.cue: 把东西都关了之后，我下班后能专心看书。
cards.task: Describe your state after work once the phone or the devices are off.
cards.answer: With everything shut off, I can focus on reading after work.
cards.said: With everything shut off, I can focus on reading books after work.
cards.why: Correct. Chose the participle route over the simpler `with my phone off`, which is the harder of the two.

cards.cue: 一个分享菜谱的平台
cards.task: 一个分享菜谱的平台
cards.answer: a recipe-sharing platform
cards.said: a recipe-sharing platform

cards.cue: 一个游戏论坛
cards.task: 一个游戏论坛
cards.answer: a gaming forum
cards.said: a gaming forum
cards.why: Day 07 produced `a game forum`, which passes; `gaming` is the idiomatic choice.

cards.cue: 一个发短信的服务
cards.task: 一个发短信的服务
cards.answer: an SMS-sending service
cards.said: a SMS-sending service
cards.why: The stack is right; the article is not. `a` vs `an` follows pronunciation, not spelling - `SMS` opens on /e/, so it takes `an`. Same class: `an FBI agent`, `an hour`, `an MBA`; and inversely `a university`, `a European`, both opening on /j/.

cards.cue: 一个监控接口的看板
cards.task: 一个监控接口的看板
cards.answer: an API monitoring dashboard
cards.said: a monitoring dashboard
cards.why: Already produced in Day 05 as a three-noun stack, unprompted, before this pattern was ever named.

cards.cue: 一本讲投资的书
cards.task: 一本讲投资的书
cards.answer: a book about investing
cards.said: a book about investing
cards.why: Content, so no stacking. Trap correctly refused.

cards.cue: 一个学投资的 App
cards.task: 一个学投资的 App
cards.answer: an investing app
cards.said: an APP about learning investing
cards.why: The one stackable item hidden among the traps. An app is built to do a job, not to discuss a topic - it is *for* investing, not *about* investing. Two side notes: `APP` in capitals is a Chinese-internet convention, English writes `app`; and `learning investing` collides two `-ing`s, which is why native usage drops one. `an app for learning to invest` is also entirely correct, just uncompressed.

cards.cue: 一场关于业务逻辑的讨论
cards.task: 一场关于业务逻辑的讨论
cards.answer: a discussion about business logic
cards.said: a discussion about business logic
cards.why: Content again. Correctly refused.

cards.cue: 一个测试短信服务的脚本
cards.task: 一个测试短信服务的脚本
cards.answer: an SMS service test script
cards.said: an SMS service test script
cards.why: Four nouns in a row, and the article corrected from item 1.3 without being told.

cards.cue: 一个讲远程办公的播客
cards.task: 一个讲远程办公的播客
cards.answer: a podcast about remote work
cards.said: a podcast about remote job
cards.why: Correctly refused to stack. Not counted against the pattern: `remote job` -> `remote work` - a `job` is the position you hold, `work` is the activity, and a podcast is about the latter.

cards.cue: 有人问你小红书是什么，你介绍一下。
cards.task: Someone asks what Rednote is. Introduce it.
cards.answer: Rednote is a life-sharing platform.
cards.said: Rednote is a life-sharing platform.
cards.why: Built a compound that was never taught, and it is idiomatic.

cards.cue: 跟同事说你们有个东西能监控服务挂没挂。
cards.task: Tell a colleague you have something that monitors whether a service is down.
cards.answer: We've got a monitoring dashboard to check whether the service is down.
cards.said: We've got a monitoring dashboard to check whether the service is down.

cards.cue: 解释你周末学投资都用什么。
cards.task: Explain what you use to learn about investing at weekends.
cards.answer: Xueqiu is an investing app that helps me keep an eye on what's happening across different industries.
cards.said: Xueqiu is an investing app which helps me keep an eye on development trends from different industries.
cards.why: Pattern correct, and it is the exact phrase missed in 2.2, self-corrected with no prompting. Not counted against the pattern: `which` -> `that` in a defining clause is the more common spoken choice, and `development trends from different industries` is a shade written for speech.

cards.cue: 通勤越长，我越不想去公司。
cards.task: The commute is long. I want to go into the office less.
cards.answer: The longer the commute is, the less I want to go into the office.
cards.said: The longer the commute is, the less I want to go into the office.
cards.why: `is` is optional - *the longer the commute, the less I want to go in* is the tighter spoken version - but keeping it is never wrong.

cards.cue: 经验越多，处理复杂 ticket 就越顺手。
cards.task: I get more experience. I handle complicated tickets better.
cards.answer: The more experience I get, the better I handle complicated tickets.
cards.said: The more experience I get, the better I handle complicated tickets.
cards.why: The noun slot (`the more experience`) built correctly on the first attempt, which is the harder of the two shapes.

cards.cue: 攻略看得越多，解锁的隐藏结局就越多。
cards.task: I read more guides. I unlock more hidden endings.
cards.answer: The more guides I read, the more hidden endings I unlock.
cards.said: The more guilds I read, the more hidden endings I unlock.
cards.why: Structure correct. Not counted against the pattern: `guilds` (公会) for `guides` (攻略) is a typo at speed, not a structural miss.

cards.cue: 同一时间订票的人越多，票就越难抢。
cards.task: More people book at the same time. It gets harder to get a ticket.
cards.answer: The more people book at the same time, the harder it gets to get a ticket.
cards.said: The more people book at the same time, the harder it gets to get a ticket.

cards.cue: AI 发展越来越快。
cards.task: AI is developing quickly, and it keeps speeding up. (no second variable)
cards.answer: AI is developing faster and faster, and it keeps speeding up.
cards.said: AI is developing more and more quickly, and it keeps speeding up.
cards.why: The trap item, and it was read correctly - `more and more`, not the frame. Not counted against the pattern: `faster and faster` is the spoken form; `more and more quickly` is correct but written.

cards.cue: 在图书馆待的时间越长，做完的事越多。
cards.task: I spend more time in the library. I get more done.
cards.answer: The more time I spend in the library, the more I get done.
cards.said: The more time I spend in the library, the more I get done.

cards.cue: 路况越差，通勤越难熬。
cards.task: The traffic is bad. The commute is brutal.
cards.answer: The worse the traffic, the more brutal the commute.
cards.said: The worse the traffic is, the more brutal the commute is.
cards.why: Both `is`s droppable here, since each half is noun + be + adjective. Yours is grammatical; the shorter one is what gets said.

cards.cue: 工作时间越长，睡得越差。
cards.task: I work longer hours. I sleep worse.
cards.answer: The longer I work, the worse I sleep.
cards.said: The longer hours I work, the worse I sleep.
cards.why: The frame is right. `the longer hours` puts a noun in a slot that does not need one - drop it (`the longer I work`) or make it countable (`the more hours I work`).

cards.cue: 同事问你为什么想远程，把通勤和你想不想去公司连起来说。
cards.task: A colleague asks why you would rather work remote. Link the commute to how you feel about going in.
cards.answer: The longer the commute is, the less I want to go into the office.
cards.said: The longer the commute is, the less I want to go to office.
cards.why: Structure correct. `to office` needs `the` - or drop the noun entirely: `the less I want to go in`.

cards.cue: 解释你为什么周末一直在读《Clean Code》。
cards.task: Explain why you keep reading Clean Code at weekends.
cards.answer: The better I want to get at my job, the more I have to read.
cards.said: The better I want to be at work, the more I have to read.
cards.why: Idiomatic use of the frame with `want`, which was not taught. `at work` means physically present; `at my job` means skilled at it, which is the intended sense - and it lands `up to the job` from Day 11 in a new shape.

cards.cue: 跟同事说，改动碰到的核心逻辑越多，测试就越久。
cards.task: Tell a teammate that a change touching core logic takes longer to test.
cards.answer: The more core logic a change touches, the longer it takes to test.
cards.said: The more complex of the file we change, the longer it takes to test.
cards.why: `of` cannot appear - after `the + comparative` the subject follows directly. `The more complex the file we change, the longer it takes to test` is the minimal fix; the answer above also reuses P001's own material.

cards.cue: 说说十一次之后你对自己英语的观察。
cards.task: Say what you have noticed about your own English after eleven sessions.
cards.answer: The more I practise speaking English, the more fluently I can speak.
cards.said: The more I practice in speaking English, the more fluently I can speak.
cards.why: Frame correct, including an adverb comparative (`the more fluently`) in the second half. `practise` takes the gerund directly - no `in`.

cards.cue: 不管路况多差，我还是开车回家。
cards.task: The traffic gets bad. I still drive back home.
cards.answer: No matter how bad the traffic gets, I still drive back home.
cards.said: No matter how bad the traffic gets, I still drive back home.
cards.why: `gets` rather than `is` was an improvement on the cue - traffic is a state that develops.

cards.cue: 不管别人说学习算不算放松，对我来说有用。
cards.task: People say learning is not relaxing. It works for me.
cards.answer: No matter what people say, learning works for me.
cards.said: No matter how people say learning is not relaxing, it works for me.
cards.why: `how` with nothing before the subject. What is being conceded is the content of what they say, not a degree, so the word is `what`. Also `no matter what people say` is complete on its own - the original's `learning is not relaxing` was already carried by it.

cards.cue: 不管多少人同时抢票，我总得回家。
cards.task: Everyone books at the same time. I need to get home somehow.
cards.answer: No matter how many people book at the same time, I need to get home somehow.
cards.said: No matter how many people book at the same time, I need to get home tomorrow.
cards.why: `how many` + noun fills the slot correctly. Not counted against the pattern: `tomorrow` for `somehow` is a content slip - `somehow` was the point, since it carries "one way or another".

cards.cue: 不管这个 ticket 多复杂，我总得从某个地方开始。
cards.task: The ticket is complicated. I have got to start somewhere.
cards.answer: No matter how complicated the ticket is, I've got to start somewhere.
cards.said: No matter how complicated the ticket is, I've got to start somewhere.

cards.cue: 不管他周一还是周三上线，我都要先好好测。
cards.task: He ships it on Monday or Wednesday. I test it properly first.
cards.answer: No matter when he ships it, I'll test it properly first.
cards.said: No matter when he ships it, I test it properly first.
cards.why: The tense trap was the clause verb (`ships`, not `will ship`) and it was avoided. The main clause is a commitment about the future, so `I'll` there - the ban on `will` stops at the comma.

cards.cue: 你决定就好，我都行。
cards.task: You decide. It is fine with me.
cards.answer: No matter what you decide, it's fine with me.
cards.said: No matter what you decide, it is fine with me.
cards.why: Supplied `it`, which is exactly what makes `no matter` legal here. The trap only catches someone who writes `No matter what you decide is fine` - see What Went Wrong for the badly-set hint.

cards.cue: 通勤越长，我越累。
cards.task: The commute is long. It wears me out.
cards.answer: The longer the commute is, the more it wears me out.
cards.said: The longer the commute is, the more it wears me out.
cards.why: Correctly refused the concession and reached for `P004`, drilled two days earlier. First cross-drill transfer in the pattern track.

cards.cue: 不管新的商业模式多特别，LLM 都设计不出流程。
cards.task: The new business model is unusual. An LLM cannot design the process.
cards.answer: No matter how unusual the new business model is, an LLM can't design the process.
cards.said: No matter how unusual the new business model is, an LLM can not design the process.
cards.why: Not counted against the pattern: `can not` is one word, `cannot`, and `can't` in speech.

cards.cue: 同事一直催你周二上线，但测试这件事你不让步。
cards.task: A teammate keeps pushing you to ship on Tuesday. Concede nothing on testing.
cards.answer: No matter how fast you want to ship it, I've got to test it properly.
cards.said: No matter how fast you want to ship it, I've got to test it properly.
cards.why: The best item of the drill. `how fast` is an adverb in the slot, and this is precisely the Day 09 standup exchange where two flat clauses were used instead.

cards.cue: 解释你为什么国庆还是回家，即使来回八小时。
cards.task: Explain why you go home over National Day even though it is eight hours in the car.
cards.answer: No matter how long it takes, I'm going home over National Day.
cards.said: No matter how long it takes, I'd go home over National Day.
cards.why: Structure correct. `I'd` makes it hypothetical; this is a real plan, so `I'm going`. Recurring habit - `I'd` also appeared for a stated intention on Day 09.

cards.cue: 说说在家办公时你怎么处理手机。
cards.task: Say what you do about your phone when you are working from home.
cards.answer: No matter what comes in on my phone, I keep it off till I'm done.
cards.said: Whenever I'm working from home, I shut off my phone.
cards.why: Correct English, and it is `E011` produced right - the Day 02 sentence *Whenever working from home* with the subject now in place. But `whenever` states a condition where the task wanted a concession.

cards.cue: 不管工作多累，你周末还是要读书。
cards.task: Tell someone why you keep reading at weekends, even when work has worn you out.
cards.answer: No matter how tired work makes me, I'll still read at weekends.
cards.said: No matter how the work wears me out, I'll read books at weekends.
cards.why: Same miss as 1.2. `wears me out` is a verb and `how` cannot concede a verb - either reach for the adjective behind it (`how tired work makes me`) or quantify it (`how much work wears me out`). Also `the work` -> `work` is `E031`, 8th hit, and `read books` -> `read`.

cards.roundName: join two sentences, pick the right wh-word
cards.cue: 不管别人怎么说，编程就是我的放松方式。
cards.task: Everyone says coding is not relaxing. It is how I switch off.
cards.answer: No matter what everyone says, coding is how I switch off.
cards.said: No matter what everyone says, this is how I switch off. Everyone says coding is not relaxing, it is how I switch off anyway.
cards.why: Two versions, both structurally correct on the pattern. `this` for `coding` is slightly off because the referent sits in the conceded clause. The comma splice in the second version is a separate issue - see What Went Wrong.

cards.roundName: join two sentences, pick the right wh-word
cards.cue: 不管 PM 把 ticket 派给谁，我都需要理解上下文。
cards.task: The PM assigns the ticket to me or to someone else. I need to understand the context.
cards.answer: No matter who the PM assigns the ticket to, I need to understand the context.
cards.said: Either way, I need to understand the context.
cards.why: `Either way` is a valid alternative and the cue was a binary choice. Not the `no matter` form but the task was to pick the right wh-word, and `either way` is arguably the better choice here.

cards.roundName: join two sentences, pick the right wh-word
cards.cue: 不管在图书馆还是在家，看书时我都会关掉手机。
cards.task: I am at the library or at home. I turn off my phone when I read.
cards.answer: No matter where I am, I turn off my phone when I read.
cards.said: No matter where I am, I turn off my phone when I read.

cards.roundName: join two sentences, pick the right wh-word
cards.cue: 不管是队列堵了还是供应商挂了，监控都抓住了错误。
cards.task: The queue was blocked or the provider was down. The monitor caught the error.
cards.answer: No matter what happened to the queue, the monitor caught the error.
cards.said: No matter what the queue happened, the monitor caught the error. The queue was blocked or the provider was down. The monitor caught the error anyway.
cards.why: First version wrong - `what the queue happened` is not a clause; `what happened to the queue` is. The wh-word introduces its own clause, and `the queue` is not the subject of that clause. Second version correct.

cards.cue: 路况很差，但我还是会开回去。
cards.task: The traffic is brutal. I still drive back. (with end-position `..., anyway`)
cards.answer: The traffic is brutal. I drive back anyway.
cards.said: The traffic is brutal, but I still drive back anyway.
cards.why: Three markers (`but` + `still` + `anyway`) for one concession. Structurally English allows it but it feels crowded. The rule is embedded in the summary now.

cards.cue: 下班后很累，但还是周末读书。用前置和后置两种说法。
cards.task: I am tired after work. I still read at weekends. (BOTH ways: front and end)
cards.answer: No matter how tired I am after work, I still read at weekends. I'm tired after work. I read at weekends anyway.
cards.said: No matter how tired I am after work, I still read at weekends anyway.
cards.why: The two versions were merged into one. `no matter` already concedes, so `anyway` is redundant. The `still` is fine with `no matter`.

cards.cue: 旧的短信供应商很可靠，但我们还是换掉了。
cards.task: The old SMS provider was reliable. We swapped it out. (with end-position `..., though`)
cards.answer: The old SMS provider was reliable. We swapped it out, though.
cards.said: The old SMS provider was reliable, we still swapped it out though.
cards.why: Comma splice between two independent clauses. `though` belongs after a comma at the end, not after the verb.

cards.cue: 周二上线还是周三上线，我都要测试时间。
cards.task: Shipping on Tuesday or Wednesday. I need the testing time. (use `either way` at the front)
cards.answer: Shipping on Tuesday or Wednesday. Either way, I need the testing time.
cards.said: Shipping on Tuesday or Wednesday. Either way I need the testing time.

cards.cue: 别人问你工作那么累怎么还周末看书。
cards.task: Someone asks how you can read on weekends when you are already worn out from work.
cards.answer: No matter how tired work makes me, I still read on weekends.
cards.said: No matter how tired I am on weekends, I still read books.
cards.why: Structure correct. The fatigue shifted from "from work" to "on weekends," which changes the meaning. Not counted: `read books` -> `read`.

cards.cue: PM 问你一个人能不能搞定这个 ticket。
cards.task: A PM asks whether you can handle the ticket alone.
cards.answer: It's a big one, but I'll figure it out anyway.
cards.said: I'll figure the ticket out anyway.
cards.why: `anyway` needs an obstacle to push against, and none was stated - alone it sounds dismissive. The learner supplied the fix himself after the drill (`It's a big one, but I'll figure it out anyway`), which is the correct version. The `either way` first given here was wrong: it needs a *choice*, and the cue had an obstacle.

cards.cue: 你在纠结国庆回不回家。两边都有代价。
cards.task: You are deciding between going home over National Day and staying in Foshan.
cards.answer: Either way, going home or staying has a cost.
cards.said: Either going home over National Day or staying in Foshan has a cost.
cards.why: `Either X or Y has a cost` is a different grammar (X or Y as subject). The task asked for `either way` as an adverbial at the front.

cards.cue: 同事问你为什么还买纸质书。用 `..., anyway` 或 `..., though` 收尾。
cards.task: A teammate asks why you keep buying physical books when you can read digital.
cards.answer: Digital books are convenient to read. I prefer physical books, though.
cards.said: Digital books are convenient to read. I prefer reading physical books, though. No matter how convenient is to read Digital books, I prefer reading physical books, anyway.
cards.why: First version correct - `C052` produced for the first time. Second version has three issues: missing subject `it` after `how convenient` (`how convenient it is to read`), `anyway` redundant after `no matter`, and `Digital` capitalised.

cards.cue: 坐在图书馆里，我才能真正专注。
cards.task: I sit in the library. I can actually focus.
cards.answer: Sitting in the library, I can actually focus.
cards.said: Sitting in the library, I can actually focus.

cards.cue: 看了日志之后，他发现 API key 是错的。
cards.task: He looked at the logs. He found the API key was wrong.
cards.answer: Looking at the logs, he found the API key was wrong.
cards.said: Looking at the logs, he found the API key was wrong.
cards.why: `Having looked` would mark the sequence explicitly, but `-ing` covers "while/by doing" and is the more natural spoken choice.

cards.cue: 在家办公时，我比在公司做得更多。
cards.task: I work from home. I get more done than in the office.
cards.answer: Working from home, I get more done than in the office.
cards.said: Working from home, I get more done than in the office.
cards.why: Worth contrasting with `E011` (*Whenever working from home*, Day 02), which is the mirror-image error: `whenever` is a conjunction and needs a subject, a fronted participle is a non-finite clause and must not have one.

cards.cue: 在传统中国家庭长大，她一直很注意健康。
cards.task: She grew up in a traditional Chinese family. She has always been careful about her health.
cards.answer: Growing up in a traditional Chinese family, she has always been careful about her health.
cards.said: Growing up in a traditional Chinese family, she has always been careful about her health.
cards.why: The hardest item of the round - the participle spans a lifetime while the main clause is a present habit, and the borrowed subject still holds.

cards.cue: 做完 ticket 之后，我就回家了。
cards.task: I finished the ticket. Then I went home.
cards.answer: Having finished the ticket, I went home.
cards.said: Having finished the ticket, I went home.
cards.why: Reached for `having + -ed` unprompted, the form most learners replace with `After I finished...`.

cards.cue: 改动碰到了核心逻辑，我得好好测。
cards.task: The change touches the core logic. I have got to test it properly.
cards.answer: With the change touching the core logic, I've got to test it properly.
cards.said: With the change touching the core logic, I've got to test it properly.
cards.why: The P001 boundary, chosen correctly - the change touches, *I* test, so a bare participle would dangle. Also `E053` produced right: Day 10 had *With the change touched the core logic*.

cards.cue: 这本书写于 1890 年，今天读起来依然很好。
cards.task: The book was written in 1890. It still reads well today.
cards.answer: Written in 1890, the book still reads well today.
cards.said: Written in 1890, the book still reads well today.

cards.cue: 大家同时抢票，票根本抢不到。
cards.task: Everyone books at the same time. Tickets are impossible to get.
cards.answer: With everyone booking at the same time, tickets are impossible to get.
cards.said: With everyone booking at the same time, tickets are impossible to get.
cards.why: Second `with` item, second correct call.

cards.cue: 面对紧张的 deadline，我砍掉了一部分范围。
cards.task: I was faced with a hard deadline. I cut the scope.
cards.answer: Faced with a hard deadline, I cut the scope.
cards.said: Faced a hard headline, I cut the scope.
cards.why: `faced` carries a fixed `with`. Dropped, it reads as an active finite verb and the fronted clause collapses. Not counted: `headline` for `deadline` is a typo.

cards.cue: 服务没人管的话，它就自己重试。
cards.task: The service is left alone. It just retries.
cards.answer: Left alone, the service just retries.
cards.said: Left alone, the service just retires.
cards.why: Not counted: `retires` for `retries` is a typo.

cards.cue: 描述你国庆开车回揭阳遇上堵车的情形。
cards.task: Describe what happens when you drive back to Jieyang and hit the holiday traffic.
cards.answer: With so many cars heading in the same direction, the traffic was brutal.
cards.said: With so many cars heading in the same direction, the traffic was brutal.
cards.why: Best item of the drill. Nothing cued `with` over a participle, and the subjects differ - cars head, traffic is brutal - so a bare participle would have dangled. Reuses his own Day 08 material.

cards.cue: 说说你在图书馆读了两小时书之后的感受。
cards.task: Explain how you feel after you have read for two hours in the library.
cards.answer: Having read in the library for two hours, I felt fulfilled.
cards.said: Having read in the library for two hours, I felt fullfilled.
cards.why: Not counted: `fullfilled` -> `fulfilled`. Correct only by accident on the form question - see What Went Wrong.

cards.cue: 跟同事说你周六查日志时发现了什么。
cards.task: Tell a teammate what you noticed when you went through the logs on Saturday.
cards.answer: Having gone through the logs on Saturday, I found our service wasn't stable.
cards.said: Having went through the logs on Saturday, I found our service wasn't stable.
cards.why: `having` takes the third form. `went` is the past simple.

cards.cue: 说说周五合上电脑之后你第一件事做什么。
cards.task: Say what you do first thing after you shut your laptop on a Friday.
cards.answer: Having shut my laptop on Friday, I went straight to the gym.
cards.said: Having shutting off the computer, I went to the gym on Friday.
cards.why: `shutting` is the `-ing`, primed by Round 1. `shut` is already the third form.

cards.roundName: rewrite with the right negation frame
cards.cue: 上线后，没有一个用户能支付。
cards.task: After the ticket shipped, all users couldn't pay.
cards.answer: After the ticket shipped, none of the users could pay.
cards.said: After the ticket, none of the users could pay.
cards.why: The Day 14 error, corrected on the first attempt. Not counted: `shipped` dropped.

cards.roundName: rewrite with the right negation frame
cards.cue: 不是所有文档都是最新的。
cards.task: Some of the team's docs are up to date. Some are not.
cards.answer: Not all docs are up to date.
cards.said: Not all docs are up to date.
cards.why: The discriminating item - partial meaning, `not all` chosen, `none of` correctly refused.

cards.roundName: rewrite with the right negation frame
cards.cue: 所有告警都没发出去。
cards.task: The queue held every alert. Zero got out.
cards.answer: None of the alerts got out.
cards.said: Since the queue was backed up, no alert got out.
cards.why: `no + noun` sibling, correct. `Since the queue was backed up` was added unprompted - a cause the cue did not state - and is also correct.

cards.roundName: rewrite with the right negation frame
cards.cue: 两个短信供应商都太贵了。
cards.task: We looked at two SMS providers. Both were too expensive.
cards.answer: Neither provider worked for us.
cards.said: Neither SMS provider was cheap.
cards.why: The polarity flip - *both too expensive* to *neither cheap* - is the elegant version.

cards.cue: 不是所有同事都看文档。
cards.task: 不是所有同事都看文档。
cards.answer: Not all colleagues read the docs.
cards.said: Not all colleagues have the right to access the docs.
cards.why: `not all` correctly chosen for partial again. Content shifted from 看文档 to access rights - a different sentence, but the negation decision was right.

cards.cue: 没有一个用户能支付。
cards.task: 没有一个用户能支付。
cards.answer: None of the users could pay.
cards.said: None of the users could pay.

cards.cue: 这项工作一点都没做完。
cards.task: 这项工作一点都没做完。
cards.answer: None of the work is done.
cards.said: None of the work is done.
cards.why: Singular verb with the uncountable noun - the decision this item was testing.

cards.cue: 我们两个人都没去过那家图书馆。
cards.task: 我们两个人都没去过那家图书馆。
cards.answer: Neither of us has been to the library.
cards.said: Neither of us go to the library.
cards.why: Frame correct. Two notes: `neither` takes a singular verb, and 没去过 is experience (`has been`), not habit (`go`).

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 重述 Day 14 的事故：优惠券 ticket 上线后，用户的支付发生了什么？
cards.task: Retell the Day 14 incident: after the coupon ticket shipped, what happened to users' payments?
cards.answer: After the ticket shipped, none of the users could pay for their orders.
cards.said: After the ticket shipped, no user could pay for their order.
cards.why: `no + noun` again, and `pay for` fixed from Day 14's `pay their orders` - a Day 14 error row repaired inside the pattern drill.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 跟同事说，事故期间监控队列把所有告警都吞了。
cards.task: Tell a teammate the monitoring queue dropped every alert during the incident.
cards.answer: During the incident, the queue was backed up and none of the alerts got out.
cards.said: During the incident, the queue was backed up and none of the alerts went out.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 有人问你们团队是不是所有人都及时更新文档。诚实回答：有人更新，有人不更新。
cards.task: Someone asks whether your whole team keeps docs up to date. The honest answer is some do, some don't.
cards.answer: Not all docs are kept up to date.
cards.said: Not all docs are kept up to date.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 你想去图书馆附近的两家咖啡店，两家都关门了。
cards.task: You wanted to try two coffee shops near the library. Both were closed.
cards.answer: Neither coffee shop was open, so I couldn't get a coffee at all.
cards.said: Neither coffee shop closed so I couldn't drink coffee at all.
cards.why: `neither` + negative verb flips the meaning - *neither closed* means both were open. The negation lives in the subject; the verb stays affirmative. This is the one miss in seventeen items, and it is the negative-polarity version of the original `all ... not` error: same scope confusion, other end of the negation family.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 国庆开车回家，高速上车流几乎一动不动。
cards.task: During the National Day drive home, the traffic on the highway barely moved.
cards.answer: None of the traffic was moving when I drove back home.
cards.said: None of the cars was moving when I drove back home.
cards.why: Grammatically fine, but the cue was uncountable `traffic` and it was converted to countable `cars`, sidestepping the decision the item was testing. Noted, not counted.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 有人问你们团队是不是所有人都想远程。有人想，有人不想。
cards.task: Someone asks if everyone on your team wants to work remote. Some do, some don't.
cards.answer: Not all the colleagues on my team want to work remote.
cards.said: Not all the colleagues on my team want to work remote.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 测试套件跑了一晚上，一个都没过。
cards.task: The test suite ran overnight. Zero tests passed.
cards.answer: No test passed overnight.
cards.said: No test passed overnight.

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: 你请了两个同事 review 你的 ticket，两人都没回。
cards.task: You asked two teammates to review your ticket. Neither has replied.
cards.answer: Neither of my teammates has got back to me about the review.
cards.said: Neither of my teammates has replied to review my ticket.
cards.why: Frame and singular verb correct. Not counted: `replied to review my ticket` reads as "replied in order to review".

cards.roundName: free production (nine items, expanded at the learner's request)
cards.cue: wiki 页面不少，但里面的信息没有一条是最新的。
cards.task: The wiki has plenty of pages, but the information in it is never current.
cards.answer: None of the information in the wiki is current.
cards.said: None of the information in the wiki is current.
cards.why: Uncountable + singular verb, landed cleanly.

cards.cue: 负责这个功能的工程师最终会来处理它。
cards.task: The engineer is responsible for the feature. He ends up dealing with it.
cards.answer: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.
cards.said: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.

cards.cue: 页面上显示的金额是他们实际花费的十倍。
cards.task: The amount was displayed on the page. It was ten times what they had spent.
cards.answer: The amount displayed on the page was ten times what they had spent.
cards.said: The amount displayed on the page was ten times what they had spent.

cards.cue: 同向行驶的车让路况变得很糟。
cards.task: The cars were heading in the same direction. They made the traffic brutal.
cards.answer: The cars heading in the same direction made the traffic brutal.
cards.said: The cars heading in the same direction made the traffic brutal.

cards.cue: 负责支付模块的同事这周请假了。
cards.task: The teammate is in charge of the payment module. She is on leave this week.
cards.answer: The teammate in charge of the payment module is on leave this week.
cards.said: The teammate in charge of the payment module is on leave this week.
cards.why: Four forms, four correct reductions, no finite verbs stranded. The adjective and PP items (1 and 4) are the branch the corpus said was missing - both landed on the first attempt.

cards.cue: 我有一台什么都能跑的机器。
cards.task: I have a rig which can run anything.
cards.answer: I have a rig that can run anything.
cards.said: I have a rig which can run anything.
cards.why: Correctly refused. `can run` is a modal + lexical verb; no reduction is possible.

cards.cue: 碰到核心逻辑的改动，测试起来更久。
cards.task: The change which touches core logic takes longer to test.
cards.answer: The change touching core logic takes longer to test.
cards.said: The change touching core logic takes longer to test.
cards.why: Lexical verb to participle - the P001/P006 boundary, correct.

cards.cue: 做支付模块的工程师请假了。
cards.task: The engineer who works on the payment module is on leave.
cards.answer: The engineer working on the payment module is on leave.
cards.said: The engineer working on the payment module is on leave.
cards.why: Same operation as item 2, spotted both times.

cards.cue: 我们换掉的那个 API 便宜得多。
cards.task: The API which we replaced was much cheaper.
cards.answer: The API we replaced was much cheaper.
cards.said: The API which we replaced was much cheaper.
cards.why: `which` is the object of `replaced` (we replaced the API), not the subject. Object relative pronouns drop cleanly - no participle, no verb change. This is the third reduction type and the only item missed in the round.

cards.cue: 你们公司某个 API 挂了的时候由谁处理？
cards.task: At your company, who handles an API when it goes down?
cards.answer: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.
cards.said: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.
cards.why: The adjective branch, produced unprompted in free production. This is the drill's main result.

cards.cue: 说说优惠券那次事故：页面上显示的金额出了什么问题？
cards.task: Explain the coupon incident: what was wrong with the amount on the page?
cards.answer: The order amount displayed on the page was ten times what they had spent.
cards.said: The order amount displayed on the page was ten times what they had spent.
cards.why: Past participle reduction - already available from Day 17, confirms the branch is stable.

cards.cue: 说说以前那个周会，以及当时你们团队的项目。
cards.task: Talk about the old weekly meeting and the projects your team had at the time.
cards.answer: Every colleague did their own thing when the weekly meeting was held because we had different, unrelated projects.
cards.said: Every colleague did their own thing when the weekly meeting held because we had different, unrelated projects.
cards.why: `different, unrelated projects` is the reduction - adjectives fronted, `which were` gone. Not counted: `when the weekly meeting held` needs `was held` - a passive-voice slip, not a relative-clause error.

cards.cue: 描述国庆开车回家时，高速上的车。
cards.task: Describe the drive home during the holiday and the cars on the highway.
cards.answer: The cars heading in the same direction made the traffic brutal.
cards.said: The cars heading in the same direction made the traffic brutal.

cards.roundName: complete with the right pronoun form
cards.cue: 我要学的东西这么多，周末根本不够用。
cards.task: With ___ (I) trying to learn so much, weekends are never long enough.
cards.answer: With me trying to learn so much, weekends are never long enough.
cards.said: With me trying to learn so much, weekends are never too long.
cards.why: The Drill 01 error repaired. `never too long` flips the cue but lands the same meaning.

cards.roundName: complete with the right pronoun form
cards.cue: PM 把这个 ticket 派给了他。
cards.task: The PM assigned the ticket to ___ (he).
cards.answer: The PM assigned the ticket to him.
cards.said: The PM assigned the ticket to him.

cards.roundName: complete with the right pronoun form
cards.cue: 决定权在我们之间，别人没有发言权。
cards.task: The decision is between ___ (we) - nobody else gets a say.
cards.answer: The decision is between us - nobody else gets a say.
cards.said: The decision is between us-nobody gets a say.
cards.why: Not counted: a bare hyphen is not an em dash.

cards.roundName: complete with the right pronoun form
cards.cue: 我妻子已经看过了，这张票是给我和她的。
cards.task: My wife has already seen the film, so this ticket is for my wife and ___ (I).
cards.answer: My wife has already seen the film, so this ticket is for my friend and me.
cards.said: My wife has already seen the film, so this ticket is for us.
cards.why: `for us` is correct - but it dodges the coordination, which was the item's purpose. The cue itself was also flawed (a wife who has seen the film cannot hold the ticket), and `for us` is the smoother way out of a broken prompt. The coordination test moved to Round 2.

cards.cue: 我周六和同事一起查了日志。换成代词再说一遍。
cards.task: I went through the logs with ___ (my colleague) on Saturday. Say it with a pronoun.
cards.answer: I went through the logs with him on Saturday.
cards.said: I went through the logs with him on Saturday.

cards.cue: 这话就咱俩知道，我觉得这个 deadline 根本不现实。
cards.task: Just between you and ___ (I/me), I think the deadline is impossible.
cards.answer: Just between you and me, I think the deadline is impossible.
cards.said: Just between you and me, I think the deadline is impossible.
cards.why: The hypercorrection item, refused. `between you and I` sounds educated to many speakers; the test was run instead of the vibe.

cards.cue: 我和他周六晚上找到了根因。
cards.task: ___ (he) and I found the root cause on Saturday evening.
cards.answer: He and I found the root cause on Saturday evening.
cards.said: He and I found the root cause on Saturday evening.
cards.why: The two-way trap held - object form after prepositions, subject form in subject position. `Him and I found` would have been the mirror error.

cards.cue: 他们谁也没回我的 review 请求。
cards.task: None of ___ (they) replied to my review request.
cards.answer: None of them replied to my review request.
cards.said: None of them replied to my review request.
cards.why: Also P007 produced again, inside a different drill.

cards.cue: 说说你平时和谁打篮球，邻居越聚越多之后是什么情形。
cards.task: Say who you usually play basketball with, and what happens when more neighbours join.
cards.answer: I usually play with my neighbours - with more of them joining, the games are fiercer than they used to be.
cards.said: I always go to play basketball with my neighbors. With more neighbors joining, the game is more fierce than it used to be.
cards.why: `with my neighbors` is a noun - the case slot never opened. `With more neighbors joining` is P001 unprompted, worth noticing. Not counted: `go to play` -> `go play`, `more fierce` -> `fiercer`.

cards.cue: 同事问为什么这个 ticket 花了两天。解释说这活是你和另一个人分的。
cards.task: A teammate asks why the ticket took two days. Explain it was split between you and one other person.
cards.answer: It was split between Jack and me.
cards.said: Because Jack and I are responsible for the different part of the project.
cards.why: `Jack and I` is the right case - for a subject. The cue wanted the preposition slot (`between Jack and me`), and the sentence was restructured so it disappeared. The case decision made was correct; the one being drilled never happened.

cards.cue: 跟别人说学英语对你个人来说很难，以及为什么周末有帮助。
cards.task: Tell someone learning English is hard for you personally, and why weekends help.
cards.answer: Honestly, English is hard for me. Weekends help because I can stay focused long enough to learn properly.
cards.said: I can stay focus on weekends so I can learn English effectively.
cards.why: The `for me` half of the cue is missing entirely. Not counted: `stay focus` -> `stay focused`.

cards.cue: 说一次你和父母在小事上的分歧。
cards.task: Describe a time you and your parents disagreed about something small.
cards.answer: When I talked through where to travel with my parents, there was a conflict between us.
cards.said: When I talked through where to travel with my parents, there was a conflict between us.
cards.why: The one item where the pattern appeared in free production: `between us`, object form, correct.

cards.cue: 负责这个功能的工程师最终会来处理它。
cards.task: The engineer who is responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.
cards.answer: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.
cards.said: The engineer responsible for the feature ends up dealing with it.

cards.cue: 上周开的会定了框架。
cards.task: The meeting which was held last week decided the framework.
cards.answer: The meeting held last week decided the framework.
cards.said: The meeting held last week decided the framework.

cards.cue: 我们换掉的那个 API 便宜得多。
cards.task: The API which we replaced was much cheaper.
cards.answer: The API we replaced was much cheaper.
cards.said: The API we replaced was too much cheaper.
cards.why: Reduction correct - the Drill 08 miss, repaired. Not counted: `too much cheaper` is not English; `too` and `much` do not stack before a comparative. `much cheaper` (便宜得多) or `far cheaper`; `too expensive` (太贵了) is the `too` slot.

cards.cue: PM 派给我的那个 ticket 涉及核心逻辑。
cards.task: The ticket which the PM assigned to me involves core logic.
cards.answer: The ticket the PM assigned to me involves core logic.
cards.said: The ticket the PM assigned to me involves core logic.
cards.why: Type 3 again, plus `to me` - the P002 case choice, correct inside a different drill.

cards.cue: 懂得多的工程师在就业市场上很吃香。
cards.task: An engineer who knows a lot is in demand in the job market. (the Day 18 boundary)
cards.answer: An engineer who knows a lot is in demand in the job market.
cards.said: An engineer who knows a lot is in demand in the job market.

cards.cue: 说说你怎么处理那些太难的书。

cards.cue: 两家咖啡店都关门了，我没喝到咖啡。

cards.said: Neither coffee shops were opened, I could not get a coffee.

cards.cue: 我请了两个同事 review，两人都没回。

cards.said: Everyone on the team have got to be responsible for this.
cards.why: The frame is right - `everyone on the team` repairs `all the team`. Two notes: `everyone` is third-person singular (`has got to`), and the Day 20 correction's second half was that responsibility here is a fact, not an obligation - `is responsible` drops the recited-rule feel.

cards.cue: 这两个因素都起作用，形成良性循环。
cards.task: All two things work. It is a virtuous cycle. (Day 20)

cards.cue: 旧短信供应商很可靠，但我们还是换掉了。
cards.task: The old SMS provider was reliable. We swapped it out anyway. (your choice of frame)
cards.answer: Both providers were reliable, but we swapped the old one out anyway.
cards.said: Neither old SMS provider is unreliable, but we swapped the old one out anyway.
cards.why: The finding of the drill. `unreliable` is a negative in disguise, so `Neither ... is unreliable` stacks two negations and forces the reader to cancel them - the Drill 07 shape in a subtler costume. Also `is` for `was`, and three concession moves (`neither ... but ... anyway`) in one sentence, the Drill 05 stacking finding. A meta question preceded this item (`reliable` 的反义词), answered briefly per drill rules - but the antonym was then used to build the double negative, which is worth recording honestly: supplying the word enabled the error.

cards.cue: 不是每个工程师都想远程，有人喜欢去公司。

cards.why: `no + noun` sibling again, and `pay for` repaired from Day 14s `pay their orders`.

cards.said: Not all the docs in the wiki are kept up to the date.

cards.cue: 描述国庆开车：车流、那些车，以及你的感受。
cards.task: Describe the National Day drive: the traffic, the cars, and how you felt.
cards.answer: With everyone heading in the same direction over National Day, the traffic was brutal.
cards.said: With all people heading in the same direction over National day, the traffic is brutal.
cards.why: `all people` is the `all the team` shape again - a bare `all` + plural noun for a specific group. English wants `everyone` or `all the people/drivers`. Third occurrence of the GROUP row gap (Day 20 `all the team`, Round 2 item 1, here). Also `National day` -> `National Day`, and `is` for `was`. The P001 frame (`with X doing`) around the quantifier was correct and unprompted - not what was being marked, but worth noting.

cards.cue: 我们当时就会知道数据库里存的金额是什么单位。
cards.task: We would have known the unit of the amount saved in the database.
cards.answer: We would have known what unit the amount was stored in.
cards.said: We would have known what unit of the amount stored in the database.
cards.why: The wh-word arrived but the of-pile survived inside the frame - "what unit of the amount". The of-phrase must unfold into a clause: subject + verb. Took three passes: first retry dropped "was" (passive participle with no be - third occurrence in two days, logged as E070), second gave the stranded "in" to "the database" instead of the unit. Final "stored in in the database" showed both locatives understood.

cards.cue: 我不知道怎么刷新我们的 API。
cards.task: I don't know the way to refresh our API.

cards.why: Grammatical - natives do say it - but the drill trains the how-frame: the way to do X -> how to do X. Landed clean on retry.

cards.cue: 我们得弄清楚告警为什么没发出去。
cards.task: We need to figure out the reason for the failed alerts.
cards.answer: We need to figure out why the alerts failed.
cards.said: We need to figure out the reason of the failed alerts.
cards.why: Both layers untouched - "reason" never became "why", and "the failed alerts" (a short de-pile of its own) never unfolded into a clause. Side note: reason takes "for", not "of". Landed clean on retry.

cards.cue: 我会在季度结束前读完它。

cards.answer: I'll get through it by the end of the quarter.
cards.said: I'll get through it by the end of the quarter.
cards.why: Correctly refused - the discriminating item. "The end of the quarter" is a property, not an information point ("什么结束?" does not exist), so no unwind. No over-application.

cards.cue: 你知道配置文件在哪儿吗?

cards.cue: 告诉我营销短信什么时候发。
cards.task: Tell me the time of the campaign SMS.
cards.answer: Tell me when the campaign SMS goes out.
cards.said: Tell me when the campaign SMS is sent.
cards.why: Correct either way - "is sent" is fine; "goes out" is the spoken default for a scheduled send. Notably the passive be was present one turn after E070 was logged for dropping it.

cards.cue: 我们更新了页面上金额的显示逻辑。
cards.task: We updated the amount showing logic on our pages.
cards.answer: We updated how the amount showed on our pages.

cards.cue: 你没看懂数据库里金额的单位,去问了同事。

cards.said: Could you tell me what unit the amount was stored in?
cards.why: The embedded frame is exact - "was" present, "in" stranded. Produced as the direct question rather than a report, which is arguably the more natural response to the situation.

cards.answer: the guy with long hair and glasses

cards.cue: 那个穿着黑色球衣的男生
cards.task: Pieces: a guy / he is wearing a black jersey
cards.answer: the guy in the black jersey
cards.said: a guy wearing a black jersey
cards.why: "Wearing" is legal English but dodged the item's decision - 穿着 takes the in-hook when pointing someone out. Also 那个 = "the". Landed on retry.

cards.cue: 那边那个正在球场打篮球的男生
cards.task: Pieces: a boy / he is playing basketball / on the court over there
cards.answer: the boy playing basketball on the court over there

cards.why: 正在做 promoted to a full verb - "a boy IS playing" is a sentence, not a phrase. Chop "is", hang the -ing. Landed on retry; "playing the basketball" lost its stray "the" (sports take no article).

cards.cue: 那边那个穿着黑色球衣、正在打球的长头发戴眼镜的男生
cards.task: Pieces: a guy / long hair + glasses / black jersey / playing on the court / over there
cards.answer: the guy with long hair and glasses, in the black jersey, playing basketball on the court over there
cards.said: a guy with long hair and glasses wearing a black jersey is playing basketball on the court over there.
cards.why: Same promotion, doubled - "wearing" + "is playing" forced a full sentence. Landed clean on retry: the full four-hook chain.

cards.cue: 那个在会上一直问问题的实习生
cards.task: 那个在会上一直问问题的实习生
cards.answer: the intern who keeps asking questions in the meeting
cards.said: the intern who keeps asking questions in the meeting
cards.why: The discriminating item passed - habitual action has no hook, correctly escaped to a who-clause.

cards.cue: 门口那个背红色双肩包的男生
cards.task: 门口那个背红色双肩包的男生
cards.answer: the boy with a red backpack at the door
cards.said: the boy with a red backpack behind the door
cards.why: Hooks right; 门口 = at the door ("behind the door" is 在门后面). Retry came back "the body" - typo for "the boy", flagged.

cards.cue: 那个穿白衬衫、正在跟经理说话的女士
cards.task: 那个穿白衬衫、正在跟经理说话的女士
cards.answer: the lady in a white shirt talking to the manager
cards.said: a lady in a white shirt, talking with the manager
cards.why: Hooks right; "the lady" (那个), and 跟某人说话 = talk to (talk with implies a two-way conversation). Both fixed on retry.

cards.cue: 客厅那台屏幕裂了的旧手机
cards.task: 客厅那台屏幕裂了的旧手机
cards.answer: the old phone with a cracked screen in the living room
cards.said: The old phone whose screen is broken in the living room
cards.why: An object's state went to a whose-clause - stiff for a thing, and it swallowed the place phrase (the screen broke "in the living room"). New hook: with + noun + -ed. Landed on retry ("the phone..." - dropped "old", noted).

cards.cue: 新同事想看你的游戏主机,你指给他看:"就是那台……"
cards.task: Your new colleague wants to see your gaming rig. Point it out: "It's the one ___."
cards.answer: It's the red one with its screen on, sitting on the desk.
cards.said: It's the red one with its screen on sitting on the desk.
cards.why: Both hooks fire; a comma is needed when the first hook already contains "on".

cards.cue: 朋友来球场看你打球,你告诉他怎么认出你:"我就是那个……"
cards.task: A friend is coming to watch you play basketball. Tell him how to spot you: "I'm the one ___."
cards.answer: I'm the one with long black hair and fair skin, in a black basketball outfit and Kobes.
cards.said: I'm the one with long black hair and white skin, in a black basketball outfit and Kobe brand basketball shoes.
cards.why: Assembly clean, adjective order right (long black hair). Vocabulary: 皮肤白 = fair skin; 科比牌球鞋 = Kobes.

cards.cue: 描述你球场或公司里最有辨识度的一个人,特征尽量多,用拆分的方式说。
cards.task: Describe the most distinctive person at your court or office - as many features as you can, the SPLIT way.
cards.answer: Mike's the one coding in the office. Long blond hair, gold-rimmed glasses, green eyes, fair skin, white shirt and blue jeans, Nikes - that's my leader.
cards.said: Mike, with long yellow hair, green eyes, white skin and a pair of glasses, in a Nike brand shoes, white shirt and blue jeans, coding in the office, is my leader.
cards.why: Every hook fired, but seven features in one sentence is exactly the overload the split exists for. Word traps inside: 黄头发 = blond (not yellow), 金丝眼镜 = gold-rimmed, "a Nike brand shoes" (a + plural; 牌 is just the brand name), "white shirt" missing "a". Retry landed the full split, all vocabulary fixed - "That's" after the dash should be lowercase, the one surviving slip.

cards.answer: The alarm went off at 9:40 pm on Monday.
cards.said: The alarm went off at 9:40 pm on Monday.
cards.why: went off is the right verb for an alarm; the stack is clean.

cards.cue: 我昨天下午 3 点左右把修复发到了生产环境。
cards.task: 我昨天下午 3 点左右把修复发到了生产环境。
cards.answer: I shipped the fix to production around 3 yesterday afternoon.
cards.said: I shipped a fix to production around 3 pm yesterday afternoon.
cards.why: 3 pm and yesterday afternoon say the same thing twice - pm already means afternoon. Pick one: around 3 yesterday afternoon / around 3 pm yesterday.

cards.cue: 复盘会定在 10 月 15 号早上 10 点。
cards.task: 复盘会定在 10 月 15 号早上 10 点。
cards.answer: The postmortem is scheduled for 10 am on October 15th. / The postmortem will be held at 10 am on October 15th.
cards.said: The review meeting will be holding at 10:00 am on October 15th.
cards.why: will be holding mixes active and passive - hold active needs a human subject (we'll hold it at 10); the meeting is held. Vocabulary: 复盘会 = postmortem, review meeting = 评审会.

cards.cue: 到上周六半夜为止，我们已经回滚了版本。
cards.task: 到上周六半夜为止，我们已经回滚了版本。
cards.answer: We'd rolled back the release by midnight last Saturday.
cards.said: We'd rolled back the release by the midnight last Saturday.
cards.why: The past-perfect trigger (by + past deadline -> 'd rolled back) was the item's real target and it landed. The error is the: midnight as a clock point is always bare - by midnight, at midnight, never "the midnight".

cards.cue: 用三个堆叠时间状语讲你昨天的一天（3-4 句）。
cards.task: 用三个堆叠时间状语讲你昨天的一天（3-4 句）。
cards.answer: I woke up around 8 yesterday morning. After getting ready, I went out with my wife at 10:30. We arrived in Zhongshan at noon. We were back home by 9 in the evening.
cards.said: I woke up around 8 am yesterday. After preparing all things, I went out with my wife at 10:30 am. We arrived at Zhongshan city at 12 am. We'd returned home by 9 in the evening.
cards.why: All three stacks structurally correct (prepositions, order, zero glue). One semantic trap: at 12 am means midnight - midday is 12 pm, safest is noon. Not counted: preparing all things -> getting ready; 'd returned by 9 -> were back by 9 (past perfect wants a reference event).

cards.why: on + line right; a specific numbered line takes no article.

cards.cue: 他依赖缓存来提速。

cards.answer: on the morning of the 15th
cards.said: in the morning on the 15th.
cards.why: Once a part-of-day carries a specific date, the whole phrase is day-bound: `on` claims the morning, the date hangs on `of` - the one legal `of` in the family. `in the morning` is only for dateless mornings.

cards.cue: 这个周日下午 2 点左右

cards.said: around 2 this coming Sunday afternoon.

cards.answer: between 2 and 4 on Friday afternoon last week
cards.said: between 2 and 4 on Friday afternoon last week.

cards.cue: 昨天中午 12 点
cards.task: Pieces: 12 / yesterday midday (meridiem trap)
cards.answer: at noon yesterday / at 12 pm yesterday
cards.said: at 12 at yesterday midday.
cards.why: Double `at`, and bare `12` is unreadable (12 am = midnight, 12 pm = noon). The Drill-14 avoidance strategy is the answer: say noon / midnight.

cards.roundName: embed the stack in a sentence
cards.cue: 我们把发布定在下周二早上 10 点到 11 点之间。
cards.task: 我们把发布定在下周二早上 10 点到 11 点之间。
cards.answer: The release is scheduled for between 10 and 11 on Tuesday morning next week.
cards.said: The press conference is scheduled between 10 to 11 next Tuesday morning.
cards.why: The range frame is `between X and Y`, never `between X to Y` (`from 10 to 11` is the frame that takes `to`). Not counted: `scheduled` wants `for`; 发布会 here is a software release - a press conference is 记者招待会.

cards.roundName: embed the stack in a sentence
cards.cue: 我昨天晚上 11 点才到家。
cards.task: 我昨天晚上 11 点才到家。(not...until frame)
cards.answer: I didn''t get home until 11 last night.
cards.said: I got home at 11 last night.

cards.cue: 复盘你的上个周末：至少三个时间堆叠，一个带上午/下午，一个用到...为止。
cards.task: Narrate last weekend with at least three stacked times, one with a part of day and one deadline (by).
cards.answer: Last Saturday, I went to charge my car with my wife at 11 in the morning. Then I drove back to my university with some friends at 4 in the afternoon. I had to be home by 9 pm, so I left early.
cards.said: Last Saturday, I went to charge my car with my wife at 11 am in the morning. And I drove back to my university with my friends at 4 pm in the afternoon. I had to get home by 9 pm so I left early.
cards.why: `Last Saturday` and `by 9 pm` are perfect, but `11 am in the morning` doubles the part of day - `am` already means morning. Pick one: at 11 am / at 11 in the morning. This exact redundancy was Drill 14''s Round-2 lesson, so it counts this time.

cards.cue: 给同事约个会：完整日期、星期几、上午还是下午、具体钟点。
cards.task: Schedule a meeting for a teammate: full date, weekday, part of day, clock time.
cards.answer: I want to book a room for the meeting scheduled for between 10 and 11 on Friday morning, November 7th.
cards.said: I want to book a room for the meeting which will be scheduled for between 10 and 11 on Friday morning next week, November 7th.
cards.why: `between 10 and 11` came out right - an hour after Round 2''s `between...to`. The miss is the date: `next week, November 7th` splits the day+date unit and double-anchors the week. Day+date live together under one `on`: on Friday morning, November 7th - drop `next week`, the date already says it.

cards.cue: 汇报一次事故时间线：警报什么时候响的，什么时候回滚的，到什么时候修好的。
cards.task: Report an incident timeline: when the alert fired, when you rolled back, by when it was fixed.
cards.answer: I received the alert around 11 pm last Friday, and we rolled back the release at 11:30 pm after we''d checked the logs. The fix didn''t ship until 1 am.
cards.said: I received the alert message around 11 pm last Friday, and we rolled back the release at 11.30 pm after we had checked the logs. The fix didn''t ship until 1 am.
cards.why: Three stacks, all correct, and the `not...until` frame self- repaired here, unprompted, an hour after Round 2 item 4 missed it. The past-perfect anchor (after we had checked) is right. Not counted: English clock times use a colon (11:30).

cards.said: at 12 on tomorrow night.

cards.said: between 9 and 10 on tomorrow morning.

cards.cue: 两周前周一早上 7 点一刻

cards.answer: at a quarter past seven on Monday morning two weeks ago
cards.said: at a quarter past seven on Monday morning, two weeks ago.

cards.cue: 直到前天中午
cards.task: Pieces: until noon / the day before yesterday
cards.answer: until noon the day before yesterday
cards.said: until noon of the day before yesterday.
cards.why: `the day before yesterday` is a stripped anchor - no `of`. The one legal `of` lives only in `on the morning/evening of + a date`.

cards.said: We had transferred data on the morning the day before yesterday.

cards.cue: 安排一次上线：完整日期、星期几、一个时间窗（between...and），用 scheduled for。
cards.task: Schedule a release: full date, weekday, and a time window (between...and), using scheduled for.
cards.answer: The coupon feature is scheduled for between 10 and 11 pm on Friday, October 30th.
cards.said: The coupon feature is scheduled for between 10 pm and 11 pm on Friday, October 30th.
cards.why: Three former misses repaired in one sentence: `scheduled for` with no stray `at`, `between...and`, day+date under one `on`.

cards.cue: 描述一次熬夜：到几点为止在干什么（by/until），几点才睡（not...until）。
cards.task: Describe a late night: what you were doing until a deadline (by/until), and what time you finally slept (not...until).
cards.answer: I was up reading a book called How to Invest until midnight, and I didn''t get to sleep until 2 am.
cards.said: I was reading a book called how to invest by 12 am, and I didn''t sleep until 2 am.
cards.why: The `not...until` half is perfect. The first half: `12 am` should be said as `midnight`, and `by` marks a completion deadline - an ongoing activity takes `until` (reading until midnight). As written it reads as "by midnight I had STARTED reading." Not counted: book titles take capitals.

cards.cue: 讲一个发生在某月某号上午的故事。

cards.answer: I was teaching my wife to drive on the morning of October 25th.
cards.said: I was teaching how to drive a car last Saturday, October 25th.
cards.why: The stack (`last Saturday, October 25th`) is a legitimate appositive. But the target slot (`on the morning of + date`) went unused - unconfirmed in production. Not counted: `teach` takes a person (teaching my wife to drive).

cards.cue: 11 月 11 号上午

cards.said: on the morning of November 11th.

cards.cue: 向团队宣布一次发布：scheduled for + 钟点 + 星期几 + 完整日期。

cards.said: A release is scheduled for 10 pm on Saturday, October 31th.
cards.why: Third clean production of this frame. Not counted: 31st, not 31th.

cards.cue: 描述一次赶工：从几点到几点（from...to），一直持续到几点（until），几点才结束（not...until）。
cards.task: Describe a crunch: from...to, until, not...until.
cards.answer: I was fixing bugs in the new project from 11 pm to 1 am, and I didn''t sleep until 2 am.
cards.said: I was fixing bugs of the new project from 11 pm to 1 am, and I didn''t sleep until 2 am.
cards.why: All three target frames in one sentence; the ongoing activity correctly paired with a range, not `by`. Not counted: bugs live `in` a project (P014 container), not `of` it.

cards.cue: 讲一个故事，必须用到 on the evening of + 具体日期。
cards.task: Tell a story and PIN the frame: it must contain `on the evening of` + a specific date.
cards.answer: The plane took off from Guangzhou to Xinjiang on the evening of October 28th.
cards.said: The plane took off from Guangzhou to Xinjiang on the evening of October 28th.
cards.why: The pinned frame landed with `on` intact - Round 2 item 3''s miss repaired in production. The route''s from...to is a correct bonus.

cards.cue: 他进门就脱掉了外套。

cards.said: He took off his suit as soon as he got in.

cards.cue: 描述你出门前的动作：关掉什么，穿上/带上什么。

cards.why: `resulted in` unprompted in free production, two rounds after it was a miss - the repair sticking. Not counted: an outage (second time today); the time stack is P013 - last Saturday evening, no `in the evening` needed.
